content: If you suspect an overdose and the individual is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. Alternatively, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If you miss a dose of your medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last updated in May 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about the product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for your specific needs. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health requirements. Common side effects of this medication may include diarrhea, headache, dizziness, drowsiness, or blurred vision. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits to you outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. If you are in the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before taking trimethobenzamide, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness, drowsiness, or blurred vision. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness or clear vision until you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Check the labels on all your medications, such as allergy or cough-and-cold products, as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness.
